title: US County Choropleth Map: CSV to Counties
description: Build a US County Choropleth Map from a two-column CSV of FIPS codes and values — 3,142 counties, five colour classes, legend included. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, paste a CSV with one row — 06037, 10000000 — and Los Angeles County takes its class colour alongside the other 3,141 counties that have data.
quick_answer: The US County Choropleth Map turns a simple CSV — one column of 5-digit county FIPS codes, one column of numbers — into a coloured map of all 3,142 US counties. Values are split into five equal-interval classes from green (low) to red (high), with a legend, in your browser.

One screaming-red county in a calm state usually means a typo, not a phenomenon. Choropleths are the best proofreaders tabular data ever had.

The line 06037, 10000000 colours Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037 = state 06 California, county 037). Leading zeros matter: 6037 would be a different, invalid code, which is why the CSV column must stay text until it reaches the tool.

If values run 0 to 100, the five classes break at 20, 40, 60 and 80. A county at 61 and a county at 99 share the top colour — equal intervals show ranges honestly but hide within-class gaps, so read the legend before the map.

faq: What class breaks should I use for skewed data?

This tool uses five equal-interval classes, which suit evenly spread values. For heavily skewed data (a few huge counties), most counties will bunch into the lowest class — that bunching is itself information, but if it hides your story, transform the values (per-capita rates usually help) before mapping.
My FIPS codes lost their leading zeros in Excel.
The classic failure. Format the column as text before pasting codes in, or re-pad to five digits (6037 → 06037). The tool expects five characters because state codes begin with 0 for nine states.
Does it handle county name changes and new counties?

The county frame follows a recent Census vintage (3,142 county equivalents). Rare changes — like Connecticut's move to planning regions — can shift codes; check the boundary viewer if a known county seems missing.
Can I download the map image?
Yes — export the finished map as a PNG for documents and slides with the Map PNG Export tool, legend included so the picture explains itself.
What do the grey counties mean?
No data in your CSV — deliberately neutral, not zero. If a county's true value is zero, include the row with 0 so it takes the low class instead of the no-data colour.
Is there a limit on rows?
The full frame is 3,142 counties and the tool is built for all of them at once. A national CSV is a few thousand lines — well within what a browser parses instantly.
